The US ETF industry is rapidly expanding:

In total, nearly 1,100 ETFs have launched so far in 2026, up +43% year-over-year.

Leveraged ETFs as a % of total ETFs launched so far in 2026 is up to a record 31.2%.

This percentage has more than quadrupled over the last 3 years. 

Furthermore, 48 thematic ETFs were launched in Q3 and 46 in Q2, more than double the previous quarterly record set in Q4 2025.

Thematic ETFs provide investors with targeted exposure to specific trends, industries, technologies, or investment themes such as AI, rather than broad-market indexes.

The ETF market is becoming more specialized and leveraged.

BREAKING: 14.5% of home-purchase agreements that went under contract fell through in September, the highest rate for any September on record.

The only higher readings occurred during the pandemic shock in March and April 2020.

By comparison, between 2017 and 2019, this metric never exceeded 12.0%.

Jacksonville posted the highest cancellation rate last month, at 19.9%, followed by Tampa at 18.8%, Las Vegas at 18.6%, and San Antonio at 18.5%.

In September, home sellers outnumbered buyers by ~63%, the widest gap on record.

US homebuyers are canceling deals at a historic pace.

Shocking stat of the day:

The combined wealth of the world’s tech billionaires surged +$845 billion in the first 9 months of 2026, the largest increase for this period of the year on record.

This brings the group's combined wealth to a record $4.6 trillion, accounting for 36% of the total wealth tracked by the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

This is despite tech billionaires representing only ~20% of all members in the index.

For perspective, billionaires outside the technology sector lost a combined -$62 billion over the same period.

Fortunes in the consumer sector fell by -$279 billion, while those in communications declined by -$92 billion.

Americans accounted for 94% of the Bloomberg Billionaires Index's total net wealth gains in the first 9 months of 2026. 

As a result, all 10 of the world's richest people have been American since September 10th, the first such occurrence since data began in 2012.

The AI boom is generating unprecedented wealth at the top.

BREAKING: Global money market funds attracted +$166.4 billion in inflows in the week ending October 7th, their largest weekly inflow since April 2020.

US money market funds alone posted +$72.3 billion in inflows, lifting their total assets to a record $8.0 trillion.

Since 2023, US money market fund assets have risen +$3.0 trillion.

Meanwhile, global bond funds attracted +$33.8 billion in the week ending October 7th.

Treasury funds accounted for +$16.2 billion, their 15th consecutive weekly inflow and the biggest weekly intake since April 2025.

Investors are piling into risk-free investments as rates surge.

We are witnessing a historic shift.

The annual spread between the S&P 500's earnings yield and the 10Y Note yield is down to -1.5 percentage points, its lowest since 2009.

Since 2022, this yield difference has fallen -440 basis points, its largest 5-year decline since the 1970s.

As a result, the S&P 500's equity risk premium is on track to post its 3rd consecutive negative annual reading, the longest streak since 2002.

This suggests that, on a yield basis, theoretically less risky 10Y Treasuries are now more attractive than the S&P 500.

In other words, investors are receiving a higher yield from Treasuries than from the S&P 500, despite the additional risk of owning stocks.

Historically, a negative equity risk premium has been associated with strong risk appetite and stretched equity valuations.

We expect an eventful Q4 ahead.

The US bull market is entering its 5th year.

Since the October 2022 low, the S&P 500 has rallied +118%, outpacing the average bull market since WWII.

This is also the 3rd-largest gain among bull markets at their 4th anniversary.

Over this period, the index has returned +21.6% in Year 1, +33.7% in Year 2, +12.7% in Year 3, and +19.4% in Year 4.

The average S&P 500 bull market's return since WWII has been +20.8% in Year 5, the 2nd-strongest 12-month performance after +39.1% in Year 1.

Of the 13 previous bull markets, only 6 lasted long enough to reach this stage.

If history is any guide, the market is heading for another year of strong gains.

The US stock market has never been this fragmented:

The 52-week correlation between the equal-weighted S&P 500 and the S&P 500 index is down to 0.67, its lowest level on record.

This measures how closely the performance of the equal-weighted S&P 500 tracks the cap-weighted index, with a lower reading indicating a growing gap between the broader market and mega-cap stocks.

The correlation has declined -0.25 points since August 2025.

By comparison, before the 2020 pandemic, this figure remained between 0.95 and 0.99 for nearly 15 years.

To put this into perspective, during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble, this metric never declined below 0.85.

The S&P 500 is more concentrated than ever.

BREAKING: US private fixed investment in information processing equipment and software is now up to a record 5.05% of US GDP.

This figure has increased +1.08 percentage points since Q3 2023.

Over this period, these investments have surged +$531 billion, to a record annual rate of $1.65 trillion.

By comparison, this percentage peaked at 4.46% in Q4 2000, before the 2001 recession.

Investment in information processing equipment and software has more than doubled since Q1 2018.

The scale of America's AI spending boom is unprecedented.
